confirmed.statement: The paper reports one experiment (S1) and no second study, pilot, or reanalysis, so the form's single study is right.
confirmed.locator: pp. 1-19, all pages read; p. 5, Sect. 3

confirmed.statement: S1 n_analyzed = 60 people. The abstract says 'involving 60 participants'. Sect. 3.1 says '60 participants were ultimately recruited' and 'The 60 participants were evenly distributed across six experimental groups, with 10 individuals per group.'

The flow diagram gives the same count and shows no loss. Fig. 1 is a raster image. Read from the extracted figure, it prints 'Recruitment and Screening (60 participants)' and 'A 3×2 group design, with 10 people per group, for a total of 60 people'. Its other panels (training, tasks, post-test, rating, analysis, outcome list) print no other count.

Every analysis keeps all 60 people. Tables 4, 5, and 6 give df_error 54 for every between- and within-subject effect, and 54 is 60 people minus 6 groups. Table 7B gives t(54) for the between-subject ART contrasts (ATP and EXP).
confirmed.locator: p. 11, Table 4; p. 12, Table 5; p. 14, Table 6; p. 15, Table 7B

confirmed.statement: The ART df of 162 also fits 60 people with four images each: 240 images minus 60 participants minus 18 within-person effect df gives 162. This is checker arithmetic. The paper prints neither 240 nor the calculation.

Fig. 3 has six panels, G1 to G6 (no, basic, or advanced design by low or high AIGC), with rows P01 to P60, ten per panel. Every row has an image in all four condition columns, and no cell is empty. The caption reads 'Overview of representative outputs from all 60 participants across four experimental conditions'.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Fig. 3 (labels read from the extracted figure image)

confirmed.statement: The counts are people, not images or ratings. Each person gave one image per condition: 'each participant submitted four representative images in total, one for each image-generation-alignment-by-prompt-type condition.' The images (240 by arithmetic) are outputs. The form leaves n_units null because the paper never prints that total, which is right.

The arms are within person, so Conditions A to D each hold the same 60 people, and the study total is 60, not 240. The paper says 'Each participant completed all four combinations of the 2 × 2 within-subjects conditions.' The form's arm counts (n_analyzed 60 each) and study count (60) are right.

n_randomized = null is defensible for the study and for each arm. The paper says only that 'task sequences were assigned using a 4 × 4 balanced Latin square design'. It never calls the allocation random and prints no count per sequence. Recruitment, grouping, and analysis all give 60 with no reported loss, so 60 would be the value if the assignment lens finds random allocation.

No exclusions or attrition are reported, so the form's 'None reported' is right. The only exclusion in the paper concerns rater training: 'a practice round on 20 motorcycle images excluded from the formal dataset'. The prompt compliance check removed nothing: 'All submitted representative outputs satisfied the operational definition of the corresponding prompt type'.

Caveat, not an error: people were screened into six cells of 10 before the experiment. The paper says '60 participants were ultimately recruited', and Fig. 1 names the first step 'Recruitment and Screening'. The group rules leave gaps (for example, more than 1 h per week of AIGC use for 3 to 6 months fits neither ATP0 nor ATP1), so a screened person in a gap could not join a cell. The paper does not say how many people were screened. This selection comes before any assignment and changes no count.

No people are shared across studies or papers. The paper has one study, and no passage says another paper uses these participants. The two studies cited as prior motorcycle research (Lee and Chen 2025; Yan et al. 2025) share no author with this paper. No other screening form mentions this sample, and a web search found no other report of it. The form's empty sample_overlap is right.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Sect. 3.2.1; p. 18 and p. 19, References; docs/creativity-screening/forms

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone: 60 people analyzed, above 50. The margin is small. The paper's own power analysis asked for about 54.

The who and country fields match the PDF. The EXP and ATP group rules in 'who' match Sect. 3.1. The acknowledgements thank 'the experimental participants from our affiliated universities'. All four author affiliations are universities in China, and the paper names no country for the participants. The text in participants.quote is verbatim on p. 5, and the locator pages are right.
confirmed.locator: p. 1, affiliations; p. 5, Sect. 3.1; p. 17, Acknowledgements

confirmed.statement: Caveat outside the counts: population 'students' is a judgement. The paper never uses the word 'students'. 'Non-design majors' and the affiliated-universities acknowledgement point to students, but EXP3 also admits 'practical experience'. The form already labels the code a judgement.

summary: The PDF supports every participant count in the c135 form: 60 people were recruited and analyzed, 10 in each of six experience-by-proficiency groups (p. 5; Fig. 1, p. 6), every ANOVA keeps all of them (df_error 54 in Tables 4 to 6), Fig. 3 shows images from P01 to P60 in all four conditions, and the paper reports no exclusion or attrition. Each within-person arm holds the same 60 people, n_randomized = null fits a Latin-square order that the paper never calls random, and no other study or paper shares the sample, so criterion 2 holds on S1 alone, while the random-order question (criterion 1) belongs to the assignment lens.
